BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r1.claim: Fearing the Lord’s station means fearing to stand before the Master for judgment on the great Day; such fear follows knowledge of creation and return.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r1.anchor: أي مقامه بين يدي مالك أمره يوم الطامة الكبرى يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى وذلك لعلمه بالمبدأ والمعاد

BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r2.claim: Maqam may be a verbal noun for standing, a place where servants stand for judgment and recompense, or an emphatic insertion.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r2.anchor: المقام إما مصدر ميمي بمعنى القيام أو اسم مكان بمعنى موضع القيام

BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r3.claim: Fear is paired with transgression because it is the first motive for obedience, followed by hope and then love; these suit ordinary people, the elect, and the most elect, respectively.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r3.anchor: جعل الخوف مقابلا للطغيان مع أن الظاهر مقابلته للانقياد والإطاعة بناء على أن الخوف أول أسباب الإطاعة ثم الرجاء ثم المحبة

BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r4.claim: Restraining the self from desire means refusing natural appetites and worldly ornament because their consequences are harmful; hawa is desire without a religious warrant.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r4.anchor: عن الميل إليه بحكم الجيلة البشرية ولم يعتد بمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزهرتها ولم يغتر بزخارفها وزينتها

BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said his greatest fear for the community was desire and long hope: desire turns people from truth, while long hope makes them forget the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r5.anchor: أخوف ما أتخوف على أمتي الهوى وطول الأمل

BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r6.claim: A great master says the seven desires listed in 3:14 reduce to worldly play and amusement, then to desire itself; escaping desire frees one from every bond and barrier.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r6.anchor: الهوى عبارة عن الشهوات السبع المذكورة في قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r7.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r7.claim: Sahl says only prophets and some, not all, of the truthful escape desire; one is safe by imposing proper discipline on oneself.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r7.anchor: لا يسلم من الهوى إلا الأنبياء وبعض الصديقين ليس كلهم

BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r8.claim: Bursevi describes the human as an isthmus between Divine and created, angelic and animal realities; from the higher aspect, a person restrains the lower self, as the Prophet addresses his human aspect from his angelic or unitive station.
BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r8.anchor: إن الإنسان برزخ بين القحيقة الإلهية والحقيقة الكونية

QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.claim: The one fearing the Lord’s station ascends to heart and witnesses divine governance, restrains the self from desire through fear or awe, and reaches paradise according to rank.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r5.anchor: بالترقي إلى مقام القلب ومشاهدة قيوميته تعالى على نفسه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r1.claim: The cited description of Judgment as a day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds explains what it means to fear standing before God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p167/r1.anchor: The day when men will rise to stand up before the Lord of the worlds

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r1.claim: A person recognizes God's station through worldly signs and fears standing before Him at resurrection.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : علم مقام الله بأسبابه في الدنيا وخاف من وقوفه يوم القيامة بين يديه

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r2.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r2.claim: The fearful have ten stations: enduring sorrow, prevailing poverty, restless awe, abundant tears and supplication, flight from ease, bewilderment, a dissolved heart, troubled life, and concord with grief.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r2.anchor: قال ذو النون - رحمة الله عليه - : مقامات الخائفين عشرة الحزن الدائم والفقر الغالب والخشية المقلقة وكثرة البكاء والتضرع

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r3.claim: Real fear distracts a person from every comfort and holds him in grief until safety from fear appears.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : من تحقق في الخوف ألهاه خوفه عن كل مفروج به وألزمه الكمد

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r4.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r4.claim: Only prophets and some of the truthful are free from caprice; desire can still overpower reason and discernment through appetites.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r4.anchor: قال سهل : لا يسلم من الهوى إلا الأنبياء وبعض الصديقين ليسوا كلهم

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r5.claim: Nothing in either world is more vile than desire that opposes truth.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : لم يجعل في الدنيا والآخرة شيء أخبث من الهوى المخالف للحق

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r6.speaker: الفضيل
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r6.claim: The best deeds oppose the lower self's desire.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r6.anchor: قال الفضيل افضل الأعمال خلاف هوى النفس

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r7.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r7.claim: One who answers this divine address devotes a lifetime to struggle and enduring opposition to the self.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r7.anchor: قال الجريري : من أجاب الله في هذا الخطاب أقبل على المجاهدة والمكابدة وأفنى عمره

SULAMI:v2p371#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r8.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r8.claim: Junayd recounts meeting a stranger who had asked God to stir Junayd's heart; the stranger said the self's illness is cured by opposing its desire, a reply he had already heard seven times.
SULAMI:v2p371#3/r8.anchor: قال الجنيد - رحمة الله عليه - : أرقت ذات ليلة فقمت إلى وردي فلم أجد ما كنت أجد من الحلاوة

TUSTARI:79:40/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:40/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:40/r1.claim: Only prophets and some, not all, of the truthful are free from appetite; freedom requires disciplining the self, and only prophets and some truthful people attain perfect discipline and character.
TUSTARI:79:40/r1.anchor: لا يسلم من الهوى إلا نبي وبعض الصديقين ليس كلهم، وإنما يسلم من الهوى

TUSTARI:79:40/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:40/r2.speaker: ابن السماك
TUSTARI:79:40/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sammak told his students that the cure they sought was to oppose their desires.
TUSTARI:79:40/r2.anchor: وخرج ابن السماك يوما إلى أصحابه وقد اجتمعوا إليه فقال لهم: قد كثرت عظاتي لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r3.claim: Fear of the Lord's station means fear of standing before Him for judgment; the possessive phrase magnifies that awe.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r3.anchor: أي مقاما بين يدي ربه يوم القيامة للجزاء وفي إضافة المقام إلى الرب تفخيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r4.claim: He says the person feared God when he was about to sin and stopped himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: خافه عند ما هم بالمعصية فانتهى عنها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r5.claim: Restraining the soul means restraining its desires, usually blameworthy; Sahl says only prophets and some truthful believers escape desire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r5.anchor: ونهى النفس عن الهوى: أي عن شهوات النفس، وأكثر استعمال الهوى فيما ليس بمحمود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r6.speaker: بعض الحكماء، عمران الميرتلي، الفضيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r6.claim: A wise saying advises opposing desire to reach right judgment; Imran's poem warns against obeying it; al-Fudayl calls resisting desire the best deed for both groups.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r6.anchor: وقال بعض الحكماء: إذا أردت الصواب فانظر هواك فخالفه.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r1.claim: مقام ربه may mean the servant's standing before his Lord on the Great Calamity and the day deeds are recalled, with the possessive construction compared to رقود حلب.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r1.anchor: أي مقامه بين يدي مالك أمره يوم الطامة الكبرى يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r2.claim: Alternatively the phrase means whoever fears his Lord, with مقام treated as extra; this rhetorically establishes fear of God, discussed at length in al-Rahman.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r2.anchor: أو وأما من خاف ربه سبحانه على أن لفظ مقام مقحم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r3.claim: Restrain the self from destructive desire by patience, preferring good works, and refusing to be deceived by worldly pleasure and ornament.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r3.anchor: أي زجرها وكفها عن الهوى المردي وهو الميل إلى الشهوات وضبطها بالصبر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil describe a person who considers a sin, recalls standing before God in judgment, fears that meeting, and abandons the sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومقاتل أنه الرجل يهم بالمعصية فيذكر مقامه للحساب بين يدي ربه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r5.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r5.claim: Al-Raghib explains the name هوا by the way desire carries its follower toward weakness in this world and the abyss in the next.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r5.anchor: وسمى بذلك على ما قال الراغب لأنه يهوى بصاحبه في الدنيا إلى كل واهية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r6.speaker: بعض الحكماء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r6.claim: A maxim says that one finds the right answer by looking at one's desire and opposing it; al-Fudayl calls opposition to desire the best deed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r6.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء إذا أردت الصواب فانظر هواك غخالفه وقال الفضيل أفضل الأعمال مخالفة الهوى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r7.speaker: أبو عمران الميرتلي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r7.claim: Abu Imran al-Mirtalli's poem warns that obeying desire or a stubborn self leads a person to ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عمران الميرتلي فخالف هواها واعصها أن من يطع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two verses concern the brothers Abu ʿAziz and Musʿab: one was tyrannical and worldly, while Musʿab feared God and restrained desire.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2.anchor: أن الآيتين نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير وأخيه مصعب بن عمير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.claim: Musʿab protected the Prophet at Uhud and died pierced by arrows; the Prophet said he entrusted him to God and recalled his two cloaks and golden sandal strap.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3.anchor: وقد وقى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بنفسه يوم أحد حين تفرق الناس عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.claim: Al-Kashshaf says Musʿab killed his captured brother Abu ʿAziz at Uhud; the account says their mother was exceptionally wealthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4.anchor: وفي الكشاف أنه قتل أخاه أبا عزيز يوم أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas connects the two verses to Abu Jahl and Musʿab; another says the first verse concerned al-Nadr and his son al-Harith.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أنهما نزلتا في أبي جهل وفي مصعب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r5.claim: Fearing the Lord’s standing means restraining oneself from forbidden desires; Muqatil describes someone recalling judgment while tempted and therefore refraining.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r5.anchor: عن المحارم التي تشتهيها، قال مقاتل: هو الرجل يهم بالمعصية فيذكر مقامه للحساب

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r4.claim: The person who fears standing before the Lord knows origin and return, and restrains desire because it leads to punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r4.anchor: { وأما من خاف مقام ربه } مقامه بين يدي ربه لعلمه بالمبدأ والمعاد

BINTSHATI:v1p157/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r2.claim: Fearing one’s Lord’s standing evokes continual awareness of standing before God, whether maqām is read as an action, time, or place.
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r2.anchor: في ذكر المقام هنا، مقام ربه، إيحاء بأن الخائف يراقب ربه في كل عمله ومسعاه

BINTSHATI:v1p157/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says attaching maqām to the Lord magnifies the station and inspires profound awe.
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r3.anchor: وفي إضافة المقام للرب تفخيم للمقام وتهويل عظيم واقع من النفوس موقعاً عظيماً

BINTSHATI:v1p157/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r4.claim: Hawā means inclination, originally likened to a raptor plunging on prey; it may draw toward good or evil, though usage is mostly blameworthy.
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r4.anchor: والهوى الميل، وربما كان أصل استعماله في: هوت العقاب إذا انقضت على فريستها

BINTSHATI:v1p158/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p158/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p158/r1.claim: The Qur’anic examples associate following hawā with misguidance, supporting the reading here as surrender to ruinous desire.
BINTSHATI:v1p158/r1.anchor: وهذا التتبع، يؤيد ما يطمئن به السياق في آية النازعات

BINTSHATI:v1p158/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p158/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p158/r2.claim: Nahā also evokes reason and sound judgment, so restraining the self from desire answers the voice of intellect.
BINTSHATI:v1p158/r2.anchor: فكما استعملت العربية ضد الأمر، استعملت "النَهَى" كذلك في العقل والرشد، ومنه

NAHHAS:v5p146/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r9.claim: Fearing one's Lord's station means fearing account for sins; restraining the self means resisting desire for what is improper.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r9.anchor: أي مقام الحساب على معاصيه ( ونهى النفس عن الهوى ) وهو الميل إلى ما لا يحسن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r4.claim: Fear of standing before the Lord means fearing the encounter or its place and time, through awareness of His kindness and majesty; such fear presupposes belief in resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r4.anchor: أي قيامه بين يدي المحسن إليه عند تذكر إحسانه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r5.claim: The soul must be restrained from every desire, since the Fire is surrounded by appetites and religious law opposes what the lower self wants.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r5.anchor: أي كل ما تهواه فإنه لا جر إلى خير لأن النار حفت بالشهوات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r6.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī defines blameworthy desire as appetite that conflicts with religious commands.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r6.anchor: قال الرازي : والهوى هو الشهوة المذمومة المخالفة لأوامر الشرع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r7.speaker: الجنيد
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r7.claim: Al-Junayd says that when the self opposes its desire, its illness becomes its cure.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r7.anchor: قال الجنيد : إذا خالفت النفس هواها صار داؤها دواءها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.claim: The rhetorical arrangement uses transgression to imply the opposite of restraint and restraint to imply rejection of worldly preference.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : أتى بطغى دليلا على ضده ثانيا , وبالنهي عن الهوى ثانيا دلالة على إيثار الدنيا أولا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.claim: The warning and glad tidings follow the proof of resurrection because judgment follows resurrection; the wise prepare for lasting reward rather than transient pleasure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.anchor: فإن إثبات البعث يقتضي الجزاء إذ هو حكمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.claim: The blame concerns choosing worldly life over the afterlife; worldly benefits that do not cost one the afterlife are not blameworthy, as the counsel to Qarun shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.anchor: فأما الأخذ بحظوظ الحياة الدنيا التي لا يفيت الأخذ بها حظوظ الآخرة فذلك غير مذموم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r3.claim: The two clauses are parallel: fearing the Lord counters transgression, while restraining the self from desire counters preferring worldly life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r3.anchor: وقوله : { من خاف مقام ربه } مقابل قوله : { من طغى } لأن الخوف ضد الطغيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r4.claim: Restraining one's self personifies it as another who urges sin; this rhetorical self-separation is illustrated by Urwa ibn Udhayna's verse about heart and conscience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r4.anchor: وهذا يشبه ما يسمى بالتجريد ، يقولون : قالت له نفسه كذا فعصاها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r5.speaker: عروة بن أذينة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r5.claim: His verse illustrates the inner dialogue by which the heart appeals to conscience to restrain the self's impulses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r5.anchor: ومن أحسن ما قيل في ذلك قول عروة بن أذينة : وإذا وجدت لها وساوس سلوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r6.claim: Hawa means what the soul desires, especially appetites or anger contrary to truth and complete benefit; since such desire is unguided, ‘without guidance’ in 28:50 is emphatic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r6.anchor: والمراد ب { الهوى } ما تهواه النفس فهو مصدر بمعنى المفعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r7.claim: The generic definite article in al-hawa denotes the class of desire.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r2.claim: ‘The station of his Lord’ figuratively conveys divine majesty and awe, naming the place of standing for what is associated with it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r2.anchor: و { مقام ربه } مجاز عن الجلال والمهابة وأصل المقام مكان القيام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.claim: The paired descriptions of remembering and the Garden use a collect-then-divide rhetorical structure; ‘the self’ has the same generic definite sense as ‘the abode.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3.anchor: وفي قوله : { يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى } إلى قوله : { فإن الجنة هي المأوى } محسن الجمع مع التقسيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r3.claim: مقام ربه is the Resurrection and standing before God; attributing the station to God magnifies its terror and effect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r3.anchor: ومقام ربه هو القيامة، وإنما المراد مقامه بين يدي ربه، فأضاف المقام إلى الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person fears God while committing a sin and therefore refrains from it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: المعنى خافه عند المعصية فانتهى عنها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r5.claim: الهوى means the soul's desires and similar inclinations, usually in a blameworthy sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r5.anchor: والهوى: هو شهوات النفس وما جرى مجراها، وأكثر استعماله إنما هو في غير المحمود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r6.speaker: سهل التستري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r6.claim: Sahl al-Tustari says only prophets and some truthful saints escape desire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r6.anchor: قال سهل التستري: لا يسلم من الهوى إلا الأنبياء وبعض الصديقين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r7.speaker: بعض الحكماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r7.claim: Some sages advise opposing one's desire to reach what is correct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r7.anchor: وقال بعض الحكماء: إذا أردت الصواب فانظر هواك فخالفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r8.speaker: الفضيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r8.claim: Al-Fudayl says the best deeds go against desire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r8.anchor: وقال الفضيل: أفضل الأعمال خلاف الهوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#6/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#6/r1.claim: The explanation of fearing one's Lord's standing is given at al-Raḥmān 55:46.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r1.claim: One restrains the self from the forbidden things it desires.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r2.claim: A person about to sin remembers standing before God for judgment and therefore abandons the sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r2.anchor: هو الرجل يهم بالمعصية فيذكر مقامه للحساب فيتركها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r5.claim: Fearing one’s Lord means fearing to stand before Him and face His judgment, and restraining desire by returning oneself to obedience.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r5.anchor: أي: خاف القيام بين يدي الله عز وجل، وخاف حكم الله فيه،

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.claim: The verses distinguish obedience from rebellion: Paradise is attained through obedience and Hell deserved for sins, against the determinists' claim.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1.anchor: تبيين حال المطيع من حال العاصي، وأن الجنة تنال بالطاعة، والنار تستحق بالمعاصي

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.claim: The Garden is earned by preferring obedience and avoiding sins; the command to restrain the self from desire includes both.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3.anchor: أن الجنة تنال بإيثار الطاعة، والاجتناب عن المعاصي

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r6.claim: Obedience and sin are acts of human beings, as the verses attribute rebellion and fear to them; this refutes determinism.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r6.anchor: أن الطاعة والمعصية فعل العبد؛ لذلك قال: (فأما من طغى)، وقال: (وأما من خاف مقام ربه) فيبطل الجبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r1.claim: The soul is the self that commands evil; destructive desire means following appetites, which one must restrain and discipline through patience and preference for good.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r1.anchor: { ونهى النفس } الأمارة بالسوء { عن الهوى } المردي وهو اتباع الشهوات وزجرها عنه وضبطها بالصبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.claim: One report says these verses were revealed about Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Mus'ab ibn Umayr: Mus'ab killed his brother at Uhud and defended the Messenger until struck by arrows.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2.anchor: وقيل : الآيتان نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير ومصعب بن عمير ، وقد قتل مصعب أخاه أبا عزير يوم أحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.claim: Fearing one's Lord's station means fearing God in this life when about to sin and then desisting.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6.anchor: أحدهما : هو خوفه في الدنيا من الله عند مواقعة الذنب فيقلع , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.claim: It may mean fearing in the afterlife the standing before God for reckoning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7.anchor: الثاني : هو خوفه في الآخرة من وقوفة بين يدي الله للحساب , قاله الربيع بن أنس ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8.claim: Restraining the self from desire means keeping it from sins and forbidden things.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r1.claim: Fearing one's Lord's standing means knowing that one will stand for judgment; the self is the commanding soul and desire is its harmful inclination.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r1.anchor: أى علم أن له مقاما يوم القيامة لحساب ربه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r2.claim: Another view describes someone about to commit a sin who remembers the coming judgment and abandons it; desire is the soul's attraction to its cravings.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r2.anchor: وقيل هو الرجل يهم بالمعصية فيذكر مقامه للحساب فيتركها والهوى ميل النفس

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r7.claim: Fearing one's Lord's station means fearing the moment of standing before Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r7.anchor: أي حذر مقامه بين يدي ربه

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r8.speaker: الربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r8.claim: The feared station is the Day of Reckoning.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r9.claim: Believers fear a station that belongs to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r9.anchor: إن لله عز وجل مقاما قد خافه المؤمنون

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r10.claim: It is fearing God when about to sin in this life, then desisting.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r10.anchor: هو خوفه في الدنيا من الله عز وجل عند مواقعة الذنب فيقلع

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r11.claim: The verse forbids the self from sins and prohibited acts.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r12.speaker: سهل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r12.claim: Abandoning desire is the key to Paradise, as this verse states.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r12.anchor: ترك الهوى مفتاح الجنة لقوله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r13.claim: People then lived when truth guided desire; a later age would have desire guiding truth, and he sought refuge from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r13.anchor: أنتم في زمان يقود الحق الهوى، وسيأتي زمان يقود الهوى الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.claim: The two verses concern Mus'ab ibn Umayr and his brother Amir: Amir was captured at Badr, identified himself as Mus'ab's brother, and was initially treated kindly until Mus'ab ordered the captors to bind him.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15.anchor: أما من طغى فهو أخ لمصعب بن عمير أسر يوم بدر، فأخذته الأنصار

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r16.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r16.claim: Mus'ab said Amir was no brother to him and told the Ansar to bind their captive because their mother had wealth to ransom him.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r16.anchor: فقال: ما هو لي بأخ، شدوا أسيركم، فإن أمه أكثر أهل البطحاء حليا ومالا.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r17.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r17.claim: Mus'ab was the one who feared his Lord's station: at Uhud he shielded the Prophet with his own body until arrows pierced him.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r17.anchor: «وأما من خاف مقام ربه» فمصعب بن عمير، وقى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بنفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r1.claim: A report says Mus'ab killed his brother Amir at Badr.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r1.anchor: وقيل: إن مصعب بن عمير قتل أخاه عامرا يوم بدر.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r2.claim: Another report says the verse concerned two men, Abu Jahl al-Makhzumi and Mus'ab al-Abdari.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا قال: نزلت هذه الآية في رجلين: أبي جهل بن هشام المخزومي ومصعب بن عمير

QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r3.claim: He says the verse concerned Abu Bakr, who unknowingly ate food earned by his servant's fortune-telling, then vomited it after learning its source.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت هذه الآية «وأما من خاف مقام ربه» في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r4.claim: After vomiting, Abu Bakr prayed that any remaining food be held in his veins; the verse was then revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r4.anchor: فتقايأه من ساعته وقال: يا رب ما بقي في العروق فأنت حبسته فنزلت: «وأما من خاف مقام ربه».

QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r5.speaker: الكلبي وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r5.claim: The verse also describes someone able to commit a sin privately who refrains from fear of standing before God.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r5.anchor: نزلت في من هم بمعصية وقدر عليها في خلوة ثم تركها من خوف الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.claim: Fear of one's Lord counters transgression, while restraining desire counters preferring worldly life; fear depends on knowledge (35:28) and causes restraint, so cause precedes effect.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1.anchor: ولما كان الخوف من الله هو السبب المعين لدفع الهوى

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.claim: The two descriptions encompass all virtues, just as the paired descriptions of Hell's people encompass all vices.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2.anchor: وكما دخل في ذينك الصفتين جميع القبائح

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.claim: A reported occasion links the verses to Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Musab ibn Umayr: Musab killed his brother at Uhud and shielded the Prophet until pierced by spears.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3.anchor: وقيل : الآيتان نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير ومصعب بن عمير

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r3.claim: Some say the surah directly continues the warning of 78:40, and its focus is the Hour and Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r3.anchor: some say that it follows directly upon the first phrase of 78:40

STUDYQURAN:79:40/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r1.claim: Maqāma rabbihi means standing before God on Judgment Day and answering for one's deeds; it can also mean the station of one's Lord.
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r1.anchor: It indicates being aware of standing before God on the Day of Judgment and answering for all of one’s deeds

STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī treats fear of standing before God as the opposite of rebellion: rebellion implies ignorance, while fear implies knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.anchor: Al-Rāzī sees this fear of standing before his Lord as the exact opposite of one who rebelled in v. 37

STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.claim: Forbidding caprice opposes preferring worldly life; fear of God leads to obedience and good deeds, while caprice leads astray.
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.anchor: one who forbids the soul from caprice is the opposite of one who prefers the life of this world

TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the one who fears God, fulfills obligations, avoids sin, and restrains disliked desires has Paradise as the abode on Resurrection Day.
TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r1.anchor: فإن الجنة هي مأواه ومنزله يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.claim: The passage divides people into two exemplary classes, introducing Hell's people first because the address targets polytheists; transgression and preferring worldly life define the former, fear and restraint the latter.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.anchor: وقدم صفة أهل الجحيم لأن وجه الكلام إلى المشركين

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r2.claim: The verse describes restraining the self from desire rather than never acting on it, since ignorance and weakness may cause a sin without arrogance and God is forgiving.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r2.anchor: وإنما أخذ في وصفه النهي عن الهوى دون ترك اتباعه عملا لأن الإنسان ضعيف ربما ساقته الجهالة إلى المعصية

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.claim: The two classes are unbelieving wrongdoers and faithful, pious people; the fate of the weak and those mixing good and bad deeds is left to God, who may forgive or accept intercession.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.anchor: وهناك غير الطائفتين طوائف أخر من المستضعفين والذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r5.claim: Maqām originally means a place or time of standing, but can mean a person's state or rank by extension, as in the cited Qur'anic uses.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r5.anchor: المقام اسم مكان يراد به المكان الذي يقوم فيه جسم من الأجسام وهو الأصل في معناه

TABATABAI:79:1-41#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:1-41#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:1-41#3/r1.claim: God's station as Lord includes the attributes entailed by lordship, such as knowledge, absolute power, dominance, mercy, and wrath; it is the source of forgiveness for believers and punishment for deniers.
TABATABAI:79:1-41#3/r1.anchor: وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم

TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r1.claim: The station feared is God's lordship, the source of mercy for faithful people and painful punishment for those who deny and disobey.
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r1.anchor: مرحلة ربوبيته التي هي المبدأ لرحمته ومغفرته لمن آمن واتقى ولأليم عذابه

TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r2.claim: One view says it is the servant's standing before God on Judgment Day to answer for deeds; the author dismisses this reading.
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد بمقام ربه مقامه من ربه يوم القيامة حين يسأله عن أعماله وهو كما ترى

TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r3.claim: Another reading treats “fearing his Lord's station” as an emphatic insertion meaning simply fearing his Lord, like the phrase “honor his abode.”
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r3.anchor: وقيل معنى خاف مقام ربه خاف ربه بطريق الإقحام

TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r12.speaker: جعفر الصادق
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r12.claim: Al-Sadiq says that knowing God sees, hears, and knows one's deeds restrains a person from wrongdoing; the author says this supports his interpretation of fearing God's station.
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r12.anchor: قال من علم أن الله يراه ويسمع ما يقول

TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r13.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r13.claim: Ali warns that following desire turns people away from truth, while long hopes make them forget the afterlife.
TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r13.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إنما أخاف عليكم الاثنين اتباع الهوى وطول الأمل أما اتباع الهوى فإنه يصد عن الحق

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.speaker: محمد الباقر
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.claim: Qummi reports al-Baqir saying that a servant who can commit a sin but leaves it from fear of God and His prohibition is rewarded with Paradise.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r2.anchor: قال هو العبد إذ وقف على معصية الله وقدر عليها ثم تركها مخافة الله ونهي الله

TABRISI:79:45-46/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r6.claim: Fearing the Lord's station means fearing to be questioned for duties performed or omitted; restraining the soul means avoiding unlawful desires.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r6.anchor: عما يجب عليه فعله أو تركه { ونهى النفس عن الهوى } أي عن المحارم التي تشتهيها

TABRISI:79:45-46/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r7.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:79:45-46/r7.claim: A person may begin to intend a sin, then remember standing for judgment and abandon it.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن الرجل يهم بالمعصية فيذكر مقامه للحساب فيتركها عن مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r1.claim: The explanation of fearing the Lord's standing is given earlier in Surat al-Rahman.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r1.anchor: مقام ربه} تقدم تفسيره في سورة الرحمن (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r2.speaker: عطاء والكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r2.claim: They report that the clause about restraining the self from desire was revealed concerning Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r2.anchor: قال عطاء (¬2)، والكلبي (¬3)، (ومقاتل (¬4)) (¬5): نزلت في مصعب بن عمير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r3.claim: It means restraining oneself from desired forbidden acts and from desires formerly followed in the pre-Islamic period.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r3.anchor: والمعنى نهى نفسه عن المحارم التي يشتهيها، وعما كان يهوى في الجاهلية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r4.claim: A person may intend a sin, remember standing before God for reckoning, and then leave the sin; Paradise is that person's refuge and destination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r4.anchor: يهم بالمعصية فيذكر مقامه على الله للحساب فيتركها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r5.claim: He says the refuge refers to Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr, about whom the verse was revealed, and then applies to anyone afterward with the same quality.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد مأوى مصعب بن عمير نزلت فيه (¬1). ثم هي لمن بعده ممن كان بهذه الصفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r6.claim: The refuge is for whoever has the described fear of the Lord and restrains the self from its desire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: يريد مأوى من وصفناه بما وصفناه به من خوف ربه، ونهى نفسه عن هواها (¬2)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.claim: These brief verses summarize negative and positive attitudes that prepare either immense loss or salvation in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.anchor: Bu birkaç kısa âyette âhiretteki büyük kaybı veya büyük kurtuluşu hazırlayan olumsuz ve olumlu tutumların çok veciz bir özeti yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.claim: Those who expect to answer to God set aside passing desires and live responsibly; they are promised great reward and salvation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r5.anchor: Allah’ın huzurunda dünyada yaşadığı hayatın hesabını vereceğini düşünerek geçici heveslerini bir yana bırakıp sorumlu bir hayat geçirenlerin büyük ödüle ve kurtuluşa kavuşacakları müjdelenmektedir

BURHAN:v1p63/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p63/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p63/r8.claim: The author suggests the singular “Paradise” in 79:41 may have driven al-Farrāʾ’s rhyme explanation, but the dual “both with branches” remains an objection to it.
BURHAN:v1p63/r8.anchor: قلت وكأن الملجىء للفراء إلى ذلك قوله تعالى ﴿ وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى ﴾

BURHAN:v2p296/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p296/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p296/r7.claim: Here desire stands for the sins the self desires; forbidding inclination itself is impossible, so the phrase means forbidding the self from following desire.
BURHAN:v2p296/r7.anchor: أي عما تهواه من المعاصي ولا يصح نهيها عن هواها

BURHAN:v2p384/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r1.speaker: جمهور الأمة
BURHAN:v2p384/r1.claim: The majority of the Muslim community holds that emphasis occurs in the Qur’an and Sunna.
BURHAN:v2p384/r1.anchor: الأولى جمهور الأمة على وقوعه في القرآن والسنة

BURHAN:v2p384/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r2.speaker: قوم
BURHAN:v2p384/r2.claim: Some deny that emphasis exists in the Qur’an, Sunna, or language, insisting that each expression must add a new meaning.
BURHAN:v2p384/r2.anchor: وقال قوم ليس فيهما تأكيد ولا في اللغة بل لابد أن يفيد معنى زائدا على الأول

BURHAN:v2p384/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r3.speaker: الملحدون
BURHAN:v2p384/r3.claim: Critics call emphasis pointless repetition and argue that eloquence requires concise wording; they suppose it reflects inability to express the intended meaning otherwise.

BURHAN:v2p384/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r4.speaker: الأصحاب
BURHAN:v2p384/r4.claim: The defenders answer that the Qur’an speaks in the Arabs’ language, where emphasis and repetition are recognized parts of eloquence and have many benefits.
BURHAN:v2p384/r4.anchor: وأجاب الأصحاب بأن القرآن نزل على لسان القوم وفي لسانهم التأكيد والتكرار وخطابه أكثر بل هو عندهم معدود في الفصاحة والبراعة

BURHAN:v2p384/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p384/r5.claim: The author says denial of emphasis in language is untenable: otherwise the term would have no known referent, and emphasis has many benefits.

BURHAN:v2p384/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r6.speaker: قوم
BURHAN:v2p384/r6.claim: Some classify emphasis as figurative because it contributes no meaning beyond the first expression; al-Tartusi records this position.

BURHAN:v2p384/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p384/r7.claim: The author holds emphasis to be literal: if the second identical ‘hurry’ were figurative, the first would be too, which is impossible because it precedes it.
BURHAN:v2p384/r7.anchor: جاز في الاول لانهما في لفظ واحد

BURHAN:v2p384/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p384/r8.claim: Emphasis goes against the default reading, so a word should be parsed as emphatic only when an independent meaning cannot be assigned to it.
BURHAN:v2p384/r8.anchor: إنه خلاف الأصل فلا يحمل اللفظ على التأكيد إلا عند تعذر حمله على مدة محددة

BURHAN:v2p384/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p384/r9.claim: The author rejects an unspecified criterion that accepts any meaning, since the meaning conveyed by a word is not itself another word-form that must imitate it.
BURHAN:v2p384/r9.anchor: وما قاله ضعيف لأن المفهوم من دلالة اللفظ ليس من باب الألفاظ حتى يحذو به حذو الألفاظ

BURHAN:v2p384/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p384/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p384/r10.claim: Technical emphasis divides into verbal and semantic forms; verbal emphasis restates the first meaning with the same word or a synonym.
BURHAN:v2p384/r10.anchor: القسم الأول التوكيد الصناعي وهو قسمان لفظي ومعنوي فاللفظي تقرير معنى الأول بلفظ أو مرادفه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r1.claim: A further kind of imaginative rhetoric makes the audience forget the simile and its figurative status; unlike the prior kind, that earlier example was explained by a rationale.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r1.anchor: وهذا نوع آخر من التخييل وهو يرجع إلى ما مضى من تناسى التشبيه وصرف النفس عن توهمه إلا أن ما مضى معلل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r2.claim: People figuratively described as rising in rank are made to seem physically high; Abū Tammām’s ignorant man imagines the climber needs something in the sky.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r2.anchor: قول أبي تمام ( ويصعد حتى يظن الجهول بأن له حاجة في السما )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Rūmī depicts the Nūbakht family as learning astronomy by literally climbing toward the stars, not by calculation, then renews the claim with still greater force.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r3.anchor: قول ابن الرومي ( اعلم الناس بالنجوم بنونو بخت علما لم يأتهم بالحساب )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r4.claim: Calling a beautiful woman the sun and saying she shades someone from the sun suppresses awareness of metaphor; the wonder depends on asserting the paradox as literal fact.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r4.anchor: لما كان لهذا التعجب معنى فليس ببدع ولا منكر أن يظل إنسان حسن الوجه إنسانا ويقيه وهجا بشخصه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r5.claim: Using a noun such as sun, moon, sea, or lion as if it named the target literally can make the wording seem to contain no simile or metaphor.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r5.anchor: فإنهم يبلغون به هذا الحد ويصوغون الكلام صياغات تقضي بأن لا تشبيه هناك ولا استعارة

DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.claim: Hawā can mean desire or lust; Dāmghānī applies this sense to each of these passages and their parallels.
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13.anchor: ونهى النفس عن الهوى مثلها في سورة النجم وما تهوى الأنفس

DAMGHANI:v1p394/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p394/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p394/r7.claim: Maqām Rabbih means standing before God; fear of this standing is linked with Paradise and heed of God’s warning.
DAMGHANI:v1p394/r7.anchor: المقام يعني الوقوف بين يدي الله تعالى قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن
